description: The bar chart illustrates the “effect” of various multilingual BERT models—specifically mBERT and XLM, each with L₂, R₂, and B₂ variants—on four morphosyntactic features: case, gender, number, and tense. The vertical axis, labeled “effect,” ranges from 0 to 20 with tick marks at intervals of 5, representing the magnitude of probing performance or sensitivity for each model-feature combination. The horizontal axis, labeled “tag,” categorizes the four linguistic features. Each group of bars corresponds to one tag, with six bars per group representing the six model variants, color-coded and labeled in the legend: light blue for mBERT-L₂, dark blue for XLM-L₂, light green for mBERT-R₂, dark green for XLM-R₂, light red for mBERT-B₂, and dark red for XLM-B₂. Error bars extend vertically from each bar, indicating variability or confidence intervals. For “case,” mBERT-B₂ and XLM-B₂ show the highest effects (~12–13), while for “gender,” mBERT-B₂ and XLM-B₂ again lead (~4–5). “Number” shows moderate effects (~2–3) across most models, and “tense” shows the lowest effects, mostly near 0–1, with XLM-B₂ slightly higher. The chart visually suggests that B₂ variants generally outperform L₂ and R₂ variants across all tags, and that case is the most strongly probed feature, while tense is the least.
